pageCache.pageTitle: English: Reading & Phonics - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
English: Reading & Phonics
Curriculum
At Sir William Burrough we teach phonics and reading based on the Read Write Inc (RWI) programme. RWI is a phonic based approach to teaching reading. It involves children learning to recognise sounds and blending them together to read words. Children are also introduced to ‘tricky’ or ‘red’ words which contain spelling patterns that cannot be sounded out. Some of the most frequently used words in the English language have an uncommon spelling pattern and must be learnt by sight. Read Write Inc. introduces the simple Speed Sounds (one sound, one grapheme or special friends: two letters, one sound) with Speed Sounds Set 1 and Set 2. The children then learn more ways of reading the same sounds with the complex Speed Sounds Set 3. Children are taught letter names before moving on to Speed Sounds Set 3. Once children know the first set of Speed Sounds they are ready to read the first Storybooks. Speed Sounds:
The children are also taught how to use their phoneme (sound) grapheme (letter) knowledge when writing. Their weekly spellings focus also reinforces this. For further information about the Read Write Inc. programme please see the website http://www.ruthmiskin.com/en/parents/
In addition to daily discrete Phonics lessons, Early Reading is promoted across our EY and KS1 curriculum. Our children enjoy a range of high-quality and language-rich texts, which they talk about, act out and explore in Literacy/English lessons, as well as in the wider provision, and across the curriculum.
Post-Phonics: Whole-Class Reading (word reading and language comprehension)
Once our children have completed the Phonics programme, demonstrating a secure understanding of the 5 skills, learners move on to our whole class reading approach:
Reading at Home
At Sir William Burrough, we are committed to fostering a lifelong love of reading in every pupil.
Children accessing phonics will take home the book they are looking at this week. This is to build fluency with the shared book from school. Children will also receive weekly QR codes to support the sounds they have been focusing on. This may include additional blending/ transcription games depending on your child’s reading level.
Children beyond the phonic programme use the Accelerated Reader (AR) program by Renaissance to support our pupils continued reading at home.
Our children are supported to choose books that are closely matched to their reading abilities (a child will have a ZPD range e.g. 3.4-5.7); a wide selection of books is kept in in-class libraries for the children to choose from. Having read a book in their reading range at home, the children are then able to do an AR quiz on that book (at home/during one timetabled slot in school). Each successful quiz gives the children points, these points then translate into book prizes to reward the children for their efforts.
All children also take home a free choice book from classroom bookshelves and an additional read for pleasure book from the library, which can be changed during their weekly library slot.
Please see our booklet here, detailing how to access AR quizzes at home:
The Oxford Language Report on ‘Why Closing the Word Gap Matters (2018), details that ‘children who had never or barely been read to, heard 4,662 words by the age of five​. In contrast, children who had five books a day read to them heard an impressive 1,483,300​ words’ Therefore, parents/carers, although your child may demonstrate increasing independence in reading at this point, please do take the time to hear your child read as much as possible as well as reading sections of the book to your child also.
5 Tips for Reading with your Child at Home
Reading Diary
It is an expectation for children to read/ or be read to daily. Please complete the reading diary to show this. Date, book title and signature to show. Class teachers will monitor this regularly to offer support to families who are not able to create home reading routines.
Thank you for your continued support with your child’s reading.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Sir William Burrough Primary School, a nurturing, inspiring and ambitious school that has been rooted in the heart of the local community for generations.
Although built into the fabric of Tower Hamlets, we are committed to helping our pupils to become global citizens. We want them to have a strong sense of self – physically, emotionally and socially – and understand the wider world, so that they are best equipped to find their place in it.
As part of University Schools Trust (UST), we are fortunate to benefit from partnerships that enrich our children’s lives beyond your typical primary school. With six world leading universities providing opportunities for our pupils they are able to dream big from a young age.
These fantastic and unique relationships help us to provide an innovative curriculum that incorporates a diverse range of educational visits and experiences, ensuring pupils are motivated and engaged. This passion for learning is the hallmark of an SWB education.
We hope our website will give you a flavour of what our pupils and their families experience during their time with us, but there is no substitute for the real thing. We hold open days during the Autumn term and welcome visits from parents and carers. If you would like to meet us to find out more, please do not hesitate to book a time through our website.
Siobhan Fehim Executive Headteacher
Sir William Burrough School Salmon Lane London E14 7PQ

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club and After-School Provision - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
SWB is delighted to operate a Breakfast Club and After School Club to support our families during term time.
Please note that both of these clubs need to be booked in advance (via the form below) and for both there is a maximum of 35 places available on any one day. Places are only available for children between Reception to Year 6 (inclusive) and will be secured on a first come, first served basis.
In addition, we will be offering free childcare provision between 1.00-3.30pm for 30 children on Fridays. The school leadership team will review the number of free allocated places on Friday, as well as both clubs, at the end of the autumn term to assess and plan if a larger provision is required.
Parents will be asked to sign up for a full term so that we can manage demand and ensure the provision remains of high quality. If you would like to cancel your child's space, please do so in writing with 4 school weeks' notice. Please write to the office admin email address (office@swbschool.net).
There will be a chance to make ad hoc bookings if there are spaces available. This will be managed by the school office.
Timings and Costs
Once your place in the required club has been confirmed via the school office you will be asked to pay for each week in advance. Payment will be required even if your child does not attend, unless there is an authorised absence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Outstanding Nursery Provision - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
Choosing the right Nursery is an important step for every family, and at Sir William Burrough Primary School we are proud to offer a warm, inspiring, and well supported start to early education. Our Nursery provides a caring environment where children feel happy, confident, and ready to explore new ideas.
With dedicated staff, a rich curriculum, and an outstanding Early Years provision recognised by Ofsted, we ensure that every child begins their learning journey with curiosity, joy, and a strong foundation for future success.
A Warm and Confident Start in Our Nursery
At Sir William Burrough Primary School, our Nursery offers children a nurturing beginning to their educational journey. We recognise the Early Years Foundation Stage as a vital period in which children develop their early understanding of the world. Our Nursery setting provides a calm, welcoming environment where children feel secure and valued from the moment they arrive.
Children are supported by qualified teachers and experienced Learning Support Assistants who work closely together to create routines that build confidence and independence. Every child is encouraged to explore, question, and develop at their own pace, ensuring a strong start as they grow into enthusiastic learners.
Ofsted praised our approach by stating that children in the early years develop a genuine love for learning and make a strong start to their education.
"Children in the early years make a strong start to their education." - Ofsted 2025
Learning Through Exploration and Purposeful Play
Our Nursery curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity and a sense of discovery. Children learn through purposeful play, hands on experiences, and carefully planned activities that build early skills in reading, writing, and mathematics. These foundations are developed in a joyful and engaging way that supports each child’s natural interests.
Expert teaching ensures that children develop key social and communication skills that prepare them for later learning. With a balance of structured sessions and free exploration, children develop independence, focus, and confidence. This early grounding in essential skills allows our Nursery pupils to move forward with enthusiasm and readiness for Reception.
"Children in the early years make a strong start to their education." - Ofsted 2025
Seamless Progression from Nursery to Reception
We are committed to ensuring that children feel emotionally settled and academically supported as they move through the Early Years. Our Nursery and Reception settings share familiar adults, routines, and approaches, creating a smooth and reassuring transition.
Children benefit from consistent relationships that help them build trust and confidence. This continuity strengthens their wellbeing and helps them progress with ease. Parents value the calm and organised structure of our Early Years provision, which allows their children to thrive. This is one of the reasons why Ofsted has rated our Early Years provision as outstanding, recognising the strength of our teaching and the progress children make.
"Children in the early years develop a genuine love for learning." - Ofsted 2025
A School Shaped by University Partnerships
Sir William Burrough Primary School is proud to be part of the University Schools Trust(UST), a partnership that connects us with some of the UKs leading universities. This relationship opens a wide range of opportunities for our school community and enriches the educational experiences of our youngest learners.
Being part of this trust means our Nursery benefits from a forward thinking approach to early education, informed by research and strong professional development for staff. Children learn in an environment that champions aspiration and high expectations from the very beginning of their schooling.
Families can feel confident that their child is starting their education in a school that is part of a respected, ambitious network committed to excellence.
Rated Outstanding Early Years Provision by Ofsted

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Miss Fehim - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
If you are motivated by being bold, making an impact and nurturing our pupils to unearth their potential then I firmly believe that this will be the right place for you.
Allow me to welcome you to Sir William Burrough (SWB), located in the heart of Tower Hamlets we are one of London’s most innovative and diverse boroughs.
My goal is to make a positive difference in children’s lives. I work in education so that I can aid in shaping their lives for the better, this is why I’m motivated by our vision to provide transformational education for all.
I was born and raised in inner London and so have an affinity with this area and the demographic we serve.
I am fortunate to of had a supportive family who encouraged me to be curious about the world around me. This led me to discover my passion for working with children from an early age. I’m driven to ensure the success of all our children by working alongside the families of our community.
It is an honour to be the Executive Headteacher of this school because I oversee a team that shares my ethos. Together we are unashamedly ambitious for our pupils.
By joining our team you will be a part of a school that is committed to ensuring the best for our pupils, their families and also one another.
No matter your role, we want you to be in a comfortable enough space to be innovative, adventurous and pioneering. Our school's ethos is centred around exploration and discovery, it is a critical time to join because you will be a part of shaping SWB’s future.
Fortunately, our vision for the future is now a part of the University Schools Trust (UST), which comes with numerous benefits and positive impacts. From bespoke professional development to the wellbeing charter, you will have access to opportunities far beyond what we could hope to offer otherwise.
If you are motivated by being bold, making an impact and nurturing our pupils to unearth their potential then I firmly believe that this will be the right place for you.
I look forward to meeting you and welcoming you to the SWB family.
Executive Headteacher

Mathematics
At Sir William Burrough, mathematics is taught every day as a core subject. All pupils, from nursery to year 6, follow the White Rose Maths small steps. This programme has been created by mathematics specialists who understand how children build conceptual understanding in mathematics using a variety of representations, opportunities for problem solving and reasoning and developing automaticity of maths facts.
Our teachers consider each ‘small step’ of learning and adapt teaching so that all children can achieve following a mastery approach. Teachers follow the concrete, pictorial and abstract approach to support the development of all pupils’ schemata and deeper conceptual understanding.
Pupils are also taught discrete maths fluency lessons, where children engage in learning opportunities that support their automaticity and efficiency when calculating in maths. For example, in maths fluency lessons, children will develop their number facts recall or mental arithmetic (e.g. doubling, halving and using known times tables facts).

Science
In KS1 and KS2, science is taught as a discrete subject each half term. Within our science ‘Units of Work’, composite tasks have been broken down into smaller component tasks to ensure a structured and progressive learning experience, where children are provided with opportunities to develop both their substantive knowledge and disciplinary knowledge alike within each unit. The children carry out at least one scientific enquiry in each unit of work, where they are given the opportunity to fully demonstrate the depth of their knowledge and skill acquisition as well as further develop their abilities to think critically and ask questions about the world around them.
To support the deepening of this knowledge and widening of pupils’ schema, children use knowledge organisers to support them in recalling and retaining key information and additionally attend trips/participate in workshops linked to their science unit of work for that term. We also draw on our local library service so that our children have access to a wide variety of texts for the science unit being studied, in their classrooms daily. Our co-curriculum/enrichment offer takes children’s learning beyond the requirements of the National Curriculum as well as providing further opportunities for the children to enhance their skills beyond the programmed units of work. For example, our children engage in a variety of STEM activities during British Science Week.
At Sir William Burrough, science is taught as a blocked subject. This means that the science unit for that half term is taught every day for one week in the half term; this learning is then revisited and revised through retrieval practice factored into our weekly timetable, allowing our children to benefit from the advantages of spaced learning and interleaving. We believe that blocking subjects provides children with the opportunity to become immersed into a topic and develop deep learning in the subject discipline: more time is spent learning and applying knowledge than transitioning between different subjects within the school day.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE and Sports Premium Funding - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
Our allocated PE and Sports Premium of £18,700 for 2023/24 has been used to support a complete reworking of the PE curriculum as we shift to using PE Passport. This has included the purchase of the new curriculum and a wide-ranging upgrade to the PE equipment in the school (£3,000). We are also using an additional £3,000 of funding to support in-school CPD for staff to allow them all to improve their PE teaching skills. The remainder goes towards employing a Choreographers in Residence (£8,000) and external PE coaching including employing a professional referee (£2,700).
Our external sport's coaches provide us a constant stream of activities such as judo, fencing, boxing, rugby, cricket and much more, enhancing and extending the experiences and opportunities available to the children. Our choreographer provides weekly dance classes involving a wide variety of modern and traditional genres, building confidence, poise and self-expression across all age-groups.
Furthermore, at lunchtime, our in-school sports coaches run competitive games across all age groups, allowing every child to undertake at the very least 30 minutes of physical activity per day. All children participate in two hours of P.E. and/or Dance each week.
Every child in Years Three and Four participates in Intensive Swimming at the London Aquatic Centre. This year, 69% of our Year Sixes were able to swim competently and confidently over a distance of at least 25 metres and using a range of different strokes, and can perform safe self-rescue in different water-based situations. All this gives every child at SWB the opportunity to develop a healthy and active lifestyle.

pageCache.pageTitle: Health Matters - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
Medicals and check ups:
Parents and teachers are entitled to request a medical if they have a special concern. Letters will always be sent to parents prior to a medical, and we like you to attend with your child. Our School Nurse draws up Health Care Plans in consultation with parents and staff for children with long-term medical conditions.
Medicines:
We do not give children medicine in school for short-term illnesses. If your child needs a lunch-time dose, we'll ask you to come to school to administer it, or defer the dose until 3.00pm. Asthma pumps and inhalers can be used in school if authorised by the child's doctor, in accordance with their Healthcare Plan. For those children who require medication as part of their Healthcare Plan, medicines can be administered by staff in school, with parental consent. When this happens, a form will be sent home with the child, detailing dosage and time administered.
Illness and accidents:
If your child has an infectious illness, please let us know as soon as it has been confirmed. If your child becomes ill at school we ask you or a responsible adult to take your child home as soon as possible. If your child has a minor accident in school he/she will be attended to by one of our trained First Aiders.
All accidents are investigated and recorded. We always notify parents if an accident has occurred, especially if there has been a bump on the head. Unfortunately, a more serious accident may occur in school, and it is vital that we can get in touch with a parent or responsible adult as soon as possible, so that the child may be taken to hospital.
It is essential that the school has an up-to-date telephone number where you, a relative or friend may be contacted. If you change your phone number, please tell the office.
View our Medical Policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: SWB Curriculum - Sir William Burrough School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Intent
Why this curriculum and what do we want to achieve for our learners at SWB?
Our school values of passion, creativity, community, improvement, motivation and growth underpin all elements of our curriculum intention at Sir William Burrough Primary School.
At Sir William Burrough, we are passionate about children reaching their full potential, having a strong sense of self and being given the highest quality experiences to support them to access ‘A World of Opportunity’. We are proud to be nurturing and growing tomorrow’s global citizens.
We are always saying to our pupils ‘You Can Do It!’ as we have high aspirations for all children. Our curriculum is designed to motivate and support children to know how to grow and improve in all areas of their development.
We delight in innovation and creativity and aim to instill a secure sense of belonging and identity in our learners, and therefore our curriculum is fully reflective of our diverse community. Our aim is to forge effective collaborative working partnerships with the whole school community, ensuring the betterment of our pupils remains at the centre of all that we do.
How do our curriculum intentions align with our school values?
Passion
All children should feel passionate about their learning. We place great emphasis on children having a go at new challenges and we nurture a ‘You Can Do It!’ philosophy for all pupils. Our goal is to develop individuals that are empowered to communicate confidently and effectively as well as think deeply.
Creativity
Our broad and balanced curriculum allows pupils to develop curiosity, express themselves in unique ways, and acquire a range of disciplinary skills to a high standard. Our lessons are designed to encourage pupils to ask questions, investigate and to find answers through their learning journey. We are passionate about providing opportunities for children to create and innovate and to gain confidence in expressing their ideas.
Community
Our curriculum helps children to see they belong in our school community and to see the benefits of working in collaboration with others, including parents and families. We aim to make the best use of local resources and experiences available to pupils in our local area, and in London more widely, to contribute to the development of our pupils’ cultural capital. At Sir William Burrough, we celebrate diversity of all forms: equality and inclusion are at the heart of our curriculum.
Improvement and Motivation
Through our carefully planned curriculum and our enrichment offer, we want children to see the world as full of opportunities that are accessible to them. We believe that all children should experience a curriculum that broadens their horizons and gives them new experiences, knowledge, skills, interests and ideas. Our curriculum ensures our children are well-prepared with the knowledge and skills required to ensure they succeed in their next stages of education, and to support them to want to engage in life-long learning.
Growth
We strive to go beyond the requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage framework and the National Curriculum, delivering a rich and varied education that motivates and inspires. Through a carefully planned curriculum we aim to ensure the sequential and layered skill and knowledge acquisition for all learners, with a clear, progressive framework that’s built on sequentially, year-on-year.
Curriculum Design and Implementation
How do we bring this intention to life day-to-day at Sir William Burrough?
Our curriculum reflects our curriculum intent. Our school values are woven throughout our curriculum and have informed its design. These have helped us to create an ambitious, meaningful and progressive curriculum.
Our curriculum takes both the Early Years Foundation Stage framework and the National Curriculum into account. It has been carefully designed by experienced and expert primary practitioners in consultation with some subject specialists to provide an enhanced and challenging curriculum. In some subject areas, our curriculum goes beyond the National Curriculum programme of study, offering broad and varied learning opportunities for our pupils.
Informed by academic research about how children learn best, our curriculum enables all pupils to achieve excellent outcomes and reach their full potential. Collaborative partnerships with other schools in the University Schools Trust, and beyond, have further contributed to the development of our exciting, challenging and motivating curriculum.
Rosenshine’s Principles
Our pedagogical approach is based on Rosenshine’s Principles of Direct Instruction.
This systematic and structured approach, which is applied in all lessons, creates a supportive learning environment where all students have the opportunity to succeed.
Rooted in research on cognitive science, the application of the principles means that our teachers are continually engaging with academic research about how children learn best. The clarity in structure within this approach also helps with the effective induction of new staff.
The Principles of Direct Instruction
Daily review (retrieval practice)
Present new materials using small steps
Ask questions
Provide models
Guide student practice
Check for student understanding
Obtain a high success rate
Provide scaffold for difficult tasks
Independent practice
Weekly and monthly review
Supporting our pupils to know more and remember more over time
Our curriculum has been carefully sequenced to support the effective development of our pupils’ schemata from EYFS through to year 6.
To ensure the continued improvement and growth of our pupils, learning in each subject progresses carefully, with teachers having a clear understanding of both pre-requisite knowledge that children need to succeed in each lesson, as well as future learning that will, in time, build upon what is currently being taught. Our curriculum is designed to ensure that knowledge and skill acquisition is layered and built on over time, supporting our pupils to make meaningful connections in their learning also. This sequencing allows for children to recognise links between prior learning and the knowledge and skills learned in the current lesson, ensuring deep learning and a secure conceptual understanding.
Our teachers understand that the building of this schema is what allows our pupils to know more and remember more over time. Our teachers and curriculum leaders receive professional development opportunities to continue to develop their own knowledge of generative learning and how to deepen understanding.
Each topic and skill have been thoughtfully planned into our curriculum mapping to ensure that teachers, curriculum leaders and phase leaders understand the journey of learning from EYFS through to year 6, and can encourage children to make connections between and across subjects, due to being well informed of the pupils’ prior learning.
As per our pedagogical approach, teachers use retrieval tasks at the beginning of every lesson, including the use of knowledge organisers, to support children to recall and make connections in their learning.
Our retrieval practice routines draw on the principles of spaced learning and interleaving to support the improvement of our pupils’ retention capacities, as well as strengthening problem-solving skills as learners are supported to understand and identify connections and differences between concepts.
Our SWB ‘Units of Work’ ensure that there are regular and effective opportunities to review and retrieve knowledge learned previously, as well as ensuring that tasks given to children are of an appropriate level of challenge for children and allow children the opportunities to apply their subject-specific knowledge and skills.
Oracy, reading and vocabulary are at the heart of our curriculum
Through our curriculum, we ensure children develop their oracy skills and acquire a wide vocabulary, supporting them to be articulate and confident in sharing their learning with others.
Supporting our pupils to be confident and effective communicators, key vocabulary to be taught in each unit is planned for too, ensuring all children are supported to acquire new Tier 2 and Tier 3 vocabulary effectively.
High-quality core texts in English further drive learning in other subject areas such as history, geography and science.
Representing our community, and diverse world that we live in, our core texts have been carefully chosen to reflect this, so to provide our learners with accurate and relatable narratives to contribute to the effective building of their schemas. Curriculum resources are thoughtfully considered, quality assured and selected to effectively support children’s progress through each subject discipline.
Our teachers carefully plan for children’s progress and help children to identify their next steps.
Progression of knowledge and skills
In KS1 and KS2, subjects are studied as discrete lessons although topics have been placed in a sequence that encourages children to make strong links across subject areas. These topics integrate knowledge across subjects where meaningful connections enhance children’s understanding of broader concepts.
The knowledge, skills and concepts that will be taught in each subject are mapped out in our subject progression grids.
The purpose of our progression grids is to support teachers to understand how each skill, area of knowledge and/or concept is built on over time in each subject, including the knowledge and skills acquired in the Early Years Foundation Stage. They allow the reader to see the skills and knowledge that have been taught ‘before’ and the skills and knowledge that will be taught ‘next’, further ensuring that learning is sequential and layered.
Our progression grids also ensure that our pupils are taught the appropriate skills and knowledge in each year group, ready to make progress as they move through the school and into Key Stage 3. In addition, they also support our staff in assessing children’s depth of knowledge/skills at the end of each unit/year, where age-related/end-of-year expectations are clearly defined for all within our mixed-age structure.
Curriculum Impact
How do we know we are achieving our intent? How do we measure this?
In English and Maths, our SATs results are consistently exceptionally high, significantly passing national levels in all areas and with a significant majority — and sometimes a majority of the year group — achieving Greater Depth in one or more of the subject areas. Year One Phonics shows exceptionally high levels of success as does the Year Four Multiplication check.
Beyond these results, the whole Sir William Burrough curriculum is designed to be high impact, exposing children to many and varied experiences and concepts and to give them the knowledge-base, skill-set and drive to learn more that will set them up for secondary school and their education beyond. Children are clearly fascinated by their learning and the experiences that they have, and partake fully in all the lessons. By the end of their time, as well as achieving the high standards in the national tests, they have also become well-rounded young citizens with a deep knowledge of a wide variety of subjects and concepts, and a firm understanding of how all these are bound together

In KS1 and KS2, our bespoke art and design curriculum is taught as a discrete subject each half term. Our carefully designed ‘Units of Work’ have been developed by expert teachers. Within our art ‘Units of Work’, composite tasks have been broken down into smaller component tasks to ensure a structured and progressive learning experience, where children are provided with opportunities to develop their substantive, theoretical and disciplinary knowledge alike within each unit. More specifically, this approach enables pupils to gain a deep understanding of artistic techniques, notable artists, and composition while creating high-quality work.
At Sir William Burrough, art is taught as a blocked subject. This means that the art unit for that half term is taught every day for one week in the half term; this learning is then revisited and revised through retrieval practice factored into our weekly timetable, allowing our children to benefit from the advantages of spaced learning and interleaving. We believe that blocking subjects provides children with the opportunity to become immersed into a topic and develop deep learning in the subject discipline: more time is spent learning and applying knowledge than transitioning between different subjects within the school day.
